summary.text: Bryan Steil is the Republican incumbent for Wisconsin's 1st Congressional District, which he has represented since 2019 after succeeding Paul Ryan. A Janesville native, he worked in Wisconsin manufacturing and served on the University of Wisconsin Board of Regents before running for Congress. He chairs the House Administration Committee and sits on the Financial Services Committee, and is seeking re-election.

paragraphs.text: Steil was born March 3, 1981, and raised in Janesville, Wisconsin, and graduated from Janesville Craig High School.
He earned a bachelor's degree from Georgetown University and a law degree from the University of Wisconsin-Madison Law School. According to Wikipedia, he worked as an aide to Rep. Paul Ryan in 2003.

Before Congress, Steil spent a decade in Wisconsin's manufacturing industry, according to his House website, first with an industrial motion control manufacturer in Beloit and later at a plastics manufacturer in Milton.
In 2016 the governor appointed him to the University of Wisconsin Board of Regents, and the Wisconsin Senate confirmed him unanimously.
He won the 2018 Republican primary for the open seat of retiring Speaker Paul Ryan, won the general election that year, and took office January 3, 2019.

In the 117th Congress Steil served as Ranking Member of the Select Committee on the Economy. He was appointed Chairman of the Committee on House Administration in 2023, and he also chairs its Subcommittee on Digital Assets, Financial Technology, and Artificial Intelligence while sitting on the Financial Services Committee.
His House website says he authored the Expanding Investment in Small Businesses Act of 2019, which passed the House 417-2 in July 2019, and the Exposing the Financing of Human Trafficking Act.
He has co-chaired the Middle Class Jobs Caucus and the Future of Work Caucus, and his House website lists him as a member of St. John Vianney Parish in Janesville.
